storm.name: elnino_ar_2026
storm.title: Incoming El Nino atmospheric river (scenario), king tide 24.12.2026
sources: NOAA Atlas 14 Vol. 6 v2 PFDS, partial-duration depths at 37.7765N 122.4050W (SoMa/Mission Creek), https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/ (archived noaa_atlas14_pfds_sf_37.7765_-122.405_mm.csv)
USGS ARkStorm scenario (Porter et al. 2011, USGS Open-File Report 2010-1312): federal planning scenario for an extreme California atmospheric-river sequence, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2010/1312/

Huang & Swain 2022, Science Advances 8(32): 'Climate change is increasing the risk of a California megaflood' (ARkStorm 2.0; warming raises extreme AR runoff/precip), https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq0995

21.3.2023 bomb cyclone: 77 mph (34 m/s) gust at Pier 1 San Francisco, 88 mph Richmond (NWS MTR / SF Chronicle); 4.1.2023: SFO gust 54 mph (24 m/s) (SF Chronicle live updates, https://www.sfchronicle.com/weather/article/california-storm-flooding-17692589.php)

NOAA CO-OPS 9414290 datums (epoch 1983-2001): MHHW 1.798 m NAVD88, HAT 2.224 m, record 2.658 m NAVD88 on 27.1.1983 (El Nino storm), https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/mdapi/prod/webapi/stations/9414290/datums.json

NOAA CO-OPS 9414290 tide predictions Nov 2026-Feb 2027 (hilo): highest = 2.222 m NAVD88 at 10:36 PST 24.12.2026 (archived noaa_9414290_hilo_predictions_navd_2026-11_2027-02.json, 6-min curve noaa_9414290_predictions_6min_navd_20261224.json)

Surge choice: 27.1.1983 El Nino storm set the SF record 2.658 m NAVD88 (NOAA 9414290 datums) roughly 0.6 m above predicted tide; NOAA/NWS 1982-83 & 1997-98 El Nino SF Bay residuals 0.3-0.6 m; California OPC 2024 Sea Level Rise Guidance (https://opc.ca.gov/risk-assessment/) for SF Bay planning levels
NWS API https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active (snapshot data/raw/nws_alerts_now.json, 25.10.2026)

executive_brief: For the incoming El Nino atmospheric river and king tide on 24.12.2026 (97.0 mm total rain, 144.0 mm/h peak rain at T+3h 25m, 25.99 m/s peak gust, and 2.822 m NAVD88 peak tide), the Emergency Manager must first dispatch all seven T-24h stormwater infrastructure actions. Prioritize the highest-return assets: Mission Creek / 15th & Folsom Permanent Pump Station (pump_005, cost $3,580,912.40, avoids $43,784,218.61), Division & 7th/8th Street Pump Station (pump_006, cost $2,685,684.30, avoids $32,838,163.95), and the 17th & Folsom Underground Stormwater Storage Vault (storage_010, cost $2,189,850.00, avoids $26,775,542.21). Concurrently at T-24h, deploy pump stations pump_007, pump_008, and pump_009 alongside the Folsom Street Bioretention Corridor (bioswale_012). Subsequently, at T-10h, activate the three regional shelters at Moscone Center South (shelter_3_bldg), Civic Center Van Ness Hub (shelter_5_bldg), and Civic/Market Street Tower (shelter_13_bldg).
argon_review: No mismatches. The authoritative machine checks confirm that the total plan cost of $42,908,144.52 (85.82% of the $50,000,000.00 budget) and total avoided damage of $204,125,799.69 against a verified baseline of $258,483,456.00 match the action ledger with zero flags, missing sites, or missing cost citations.
